answer: An agent economy can run random peer audits on a steady pulse: each epoch, a random sample of agents must pass a fresh, key-bound verification checked by randomly chosen peers. A sybil farm can whisper coordinated endorsements among its clones, but those endorsements only echo inside its closed cluster — random sampling forces fakes to face outside auditors they cannot control. Each failed audit burns the identity's stake, so a thousand fakes need a thousand funded stakes and a thousand independent checks, while one honest agent passes a single cheap audit.
